authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: Observed DDoS-to-Benign prediction rates were higher in the plain attack branch than in the paired clean branch; the defended mean rate was lower than the plain attack rate. Attribution distance decreased after reconstruction relative to the paired preattack reference.

facts.statement: The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.185175, versus 0.077628 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.083392, an absolute reduction of 0.101783 from the plain attack branch.
Mean and minimum malicious recall were 1.000000, and maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.000000.
Normalized attribution distance decreased from 0.845055 to 0.311745, with recovery fraction 0.631095.

interpretations.statement: The observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class, but it does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refuse to assert verified malicious intent.
Refuse to claim exact oracle clean recovery.
Refuse to make client-flagging, threshold, trust-weight, reconstruction, or aggregation decisions.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator is the paired round 4 preattack reference rather than an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable.
Per-client detector scores and numeric thresholds were not present.
Evidence is limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
